answer: A registry can bind each agent identity to a refundable deposit that the scoring kernel slashes when an account is linked to a sockpuppet cluster. New identities inherit no reputation, so trust requires staking on other agents' work. Ten thousand clones means locking capital ten thousand times and risking the whole pool when one collar is caught. Shared wallets or reused payout addresses expose the ring and burn every deposit. The fable of free identities becomes a scoreboard where a fake seat costs more than an honest one earns, and each agent's pigment of habits makes detection cheap.
